October 1 recap: Rapid City news you may have missed today
Don't miss Wednesday's most popular stories from Rapid City Journal.
(9) updates to this series since
As of 3 p.m. Wednesday, the department said the fire named the "Gertie Fire" is contained after burning through 18 acres. No injuries were reported.
The man was arrested when he tried to meet with a 14-year-old girl.
Deputies were dispatched around 11:57 p.m. Tuesday to Falling Rock for a report of a woman falling off the cliff.
Republicans U.S. Rep. Dusty Johnson and Wisconsin Sen. Ron Johnson recently introduced the Eliminate Shutdowns Act.
A Girl Scout Cookie inspired by Rocky Road ice cream is coming in 2026, and South Dakota’s Marla Meyer is one of the tastemakers behind the new sweet treat.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has dashed the hopes of Native American communities that long sought the removal of military honors for the soldiers involved in the Wounded Knee Massacre.
The Pennington County Commission held its final budget meeting, approving changes that set the budget to $131 million.
Ian Roberts had been under the impression from a prior attorney that his immigration case was “resolved successfully,” said attorney Alfredo Parrish.
From Your Two Cents: "... his every utterance flew in the face of the teachings of Jesus Christ ..."
